Afton.label: 28 backpack / walk-in sites
Afton.breakdown: 27 main backpack sites + 1 separate walk-in site. Two group camps are separate.
Afton.note: The separate site is accessible on foot or from the river. Inventory is not nightly availability.

Lake Maria.label: 17 backpack sites
Lake Maria.note: DNR alert lists B1 closed as of August 22, 2026. Seventeen is the park inventory, not the number currently open or available.

Sand Dunes SF.label: 6 mapped walk-in sites
Sand Dunes SF.breakdown: Ann Lake sites 31–36 are the six mapped walk-ins. Dispersed camping has no fixed site count.
Sand Dunes SF.note: The DNR campground map and 2017 forest appendix support six walk-ins. The current forest overview does not repeat that breakdown; confirm the operational count with Lake Maria State Park.

Cleary Lake Regional.label: 14 walk-in sites
Cleary Lake Regional.breakdown: Basswood: 14 walk-in sites. White Pine: 6 drive-in sites. Two RV sites and 3 group camps are separate.
Cleary Lake Regional.note: The page introduction says 25 tent sites, but its detailed breakdown and April 29, 2026 map identify 14 Basswood walk-ins. Do not use the headline as a walk-in count.
Cleary Lake Regional.quote: Basswood has 14 camp sites and two RV sites.

Nerstrand Big Woods.label: 4 walk-in + 6 cart-in sites
Nerstrand Big Woods.breakdown: 4 walk-in sites + 6 cart-in sites = 10 sites reached on foot.
Nerstrand Big Woods.note: The earlier guide omitted the cart-in category. These are separate from the drive-in campground.
Nerstrand Big Woods.quote: Six rustic sites, located 150 to 200 feet from parking.

Wild River.label: 8 backpack sites
Wild River.breakdown: Aspen Knob, Breezy Valley, Buck Hill, Deer Creek, Dry Creek Hollow, Meadow Vista, Pine Ridge and Spring Creek.
Wild River.note: Four canoe-in sites and nine walk-to group camps are separate categories. The guide previously described only six backpack sites.

Frontenac.label: 2 backpack + 6 cart-in sites
Frontenac.breakdown: 2 backpack sites + 6 cart-in sites = 8 sites reached on foot.
Frontenac.note: The guide previously had only two individual cart-in descriptions and one entry covering both backpack sites. DNR says neither backpack site is good for hammock camping.
Frontenac.quote: Two backpack sites located one and one-quarter miles from the designated parking lot at the ranger station.

Sakatah Lake.label: Drive-in / bike-in camping
Sakatah Lake.breakdown: No individual backpack or walk-in category in the current DNR inventory. Five bike-in sites are restricted to campers arriving by bike without motor vehicles.
Sakatah Lake.note: Site 3 in this guide is a drive-in site. Do not count it or the bike-only sites as hike-in inventory.

Lake Elmo Park Reserve.label: 5 hike-in sites
Lake Elmo Park Reserve.breakdown: 5 individual hike-in tent sites + 3 separate walk-to group sites.
Lake Elmo Park Reserve.note: The hike-in count was correct, but the guide covered the five sites in one entry. One tent per individual hike-in site.
Lake Elmo Park Reserve.quote: Five hike-in tent sites. One tent per site.

MN Valley SRA.label: Hike-in count unknown
MN Valley SRA.breakdown: The old eight-walk-in claim is historical, not verified current inventory. Current DNR camping information lists only six equestrian sites.
MN Valley SRA.note: The current map also shows the equestrian campground without the old walk-in category. Ask DNR at 651-259-5774 whether any individual hike-in or backcountry campsites remain open before planning an overnight.
MN Valley SRA.quote: Six equestrian sites are available seasonally, from April to November.

Crow-Hassan Park Reserve.label: 2 named group camps
Crow-Hassan Park Reserve.breakdown: Bluestem and Riverbend are the two named group camps.
Crow-Hassan Park Reserve.note: Current official page does not establish an individual backpack/hike-in inventory. Group camps and horse camping are not counted as individual hike-in sites.
Crow-Hassan Park Reserve.quote: The Blue Stem and Riverbend group camps can accommodate horses.

William O'Brien.label: 2 walk-in sites
William O'Brien.breakdown: Walk-in sites 130 and 131, beside Wedge Hill Group Campsites. Four group camps are separate.
William O'Brien.note: The two walk-ins appear in DNR park notes even though the main camping-category summary omits them.
William O'Brien.quote: Walk-in sites 130 and 131 are located next to the Wedge Hill Group Campsites.

Cannon River Wilderness Area.label: 4 primitive campsites
Cannon River Wilderness Area.breakdown: Four primitive first-come campsites; no reservations.
Cannon River Wilderness Area.note: The guide represents these in one area entry. Individual site suitability is not yet surveyed.

Rum River State Forest.label: Dispersed camping
Rum River State Forest.breakdown: Dispersed camping is not a numbered campground inventory.
Rum River State Forest.note: Do not turn one forest entry into a count of one campsite, or estimate how many dispersed spots exist.

St. Croix Riverway (NPS).label: Paddle-access campsites
St. Croix Riverway (NPS).breakdown: River campsite inventory is separate from backpack/hike-in camping.
St. Croix Riverway (NPS).note: Removed the unsupported blanket count of 13. Current NPS maps distinguish individual shoreline sites, group sites and the Eagle’s Nest cluster. A current campsite total for the former loosely defined stretch remains unknown.
St. Croix Riverway (NPS).quote: These campsites are often only accessible from the water

Stanley Eddy Park Reserve.label: 12 backcountry sites
Stanley Eddy Park Reserve.breakdown: 7 campsite symbols on the North Unit map + 5 on the South/Alama map = 12.
Stanley Eddy Park Reserve.note: The county explicitly confirms 12 backcountry campsites. The old guide bundled them into one entry.

St. Croix / Chengwatana SF.label: Drive-in + dispersed camping
St. Croix / Chengwatana SF.breakdown: Boulder and Snake River are drive-in campgrounds. Dispersed camping has no fixed inventory.
St. Croix / Chengwatana SF.note: These forest entries are alternatives to designated backpack sites, not a count of hike-in campsites.

Gov. Knowles SF (WI).label: 9 primitive hike-in sites
Gov. Knowles SF (WI).breakdown: Nine primitive campsites along hiking trails, separate from the developed campgrounds.
Gov. Knowles SF (WI).note: One guide entry covers the whole category; the confirmed hammock report is for Randall Creek, not all nine sites.
Gov. Knowles SF (WI).quote: nine primitive campsites along the hiking trails
